global_status.statement: Exact reductions and certificates plus bounded exhaustive searches; no global k=5 witness or impossibility theorem.

verified_claims.claim: an ERDOS-885 K_(5,5) witness transposes to a K_(6,4) factor-difference packet
the displayed integer packets are exact: a K_(6,3) precursor, a transposed K_(4,5), and a K_(4,4)
no K_(6,4) and no K_(5,4) exists over every canonical anchor 0 <= p < q <= 6000, every compatible row, every four-row subset — 0 and 0 hits across 18003000 canonical anchors
that finite search implies the bounded necessary condition sqrt(d0^2 + 4*N_min) > 3000, equivalently d0^2 + 4*N_min > 9,000,000
across the 71 archived public 4x6 packets, root-to-positive-shift and positive-shift-to-root are exact on all 71, and 426 five-root subsets produced 0 fifth-difference hits
verified_claims.kind: closure audit over a snapshotted public dataset

explicit_non_claims: ERDOS-885 k=5 is not solved here
search exclusions are exhaustive only inside their stated bounds and relative to the checked implementations; they are not global impossibility theorems
the direct search yields a bounded necessary condition, not a global obstruction
literature novelty is not claimed; in particular the main K_(6,3) packet independently rediscovered here is already present on Thomas Egense's public 2019 4x6 square-sumset page
a no-hit result at one level does not assert uniqueness at that level
